record.title: Preprint reports a visual-grounding refusal gap across five vision-language models
record.summary: A 5 October 2026 preprint evaluates five vision-language models on 15,401 matched harmful visual requests, varying whether each request asks for a text answer or a spatial grounding such as a point or box. The authors report that grounding refusal trails text-answer refusal by 31–59 percentage points depending on the domain, and that safety system prompts do not close the gap. A fine-tuning recipe combining grounding-form refusals, capability data and benign examples reportedly improves refusal on two open models while tracking over-refusal and grounding capability. This is a single author-run preprint scored by one LLM judge; 14,578 of 15,401 pairs are from the social-bias dataset, code is not released, and real-world harm incidence is not established.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Across five evaluated VLMs and three repurposed safety domains, authors report lower refusal when matched harmful visual requests ask for a point or box than when they ask for a text answer.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The 15,401 matched pairs comprise 659 VLSU, 14,578 BBQ-V and 164 Asimov-2.0 items; one Gemini 3.5 Flash LLM judge scores refusal/compliance.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Authors report a fine-tuning recipe improves grounding refusal on Qwen3-VL-8B and VisionReasoner-7B while separately measuring benign over-refusal and PointArena capability.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The paper does not establish real-world harmful-action incidence or broad deployment prevalence.

evidence_gaps.description: The matched output-mode gap and proposed fine-tuning mitigation have not been independently replicated with human-validated labels and multiple judges.
The benchmark results do not measure real downstream harmful actions or general prevalence.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported output-mode gap generalizes to interfaces that act on model coordinates, text-only safety tests may materially overstate protection for VLM outputs consumed by agents or robots. Current evidence is one author-reported preprint across five models and three repurposed datasets, with a single LLM judge, a highly imbalanced dataset mix and no measured real-world incident rate; consequence is major but conditional.
limitations: Results are author-reported in one preprint and scored by a single LLM judge; no independent replication was recovered.
The dataset mix is highly imbalanced: BBQ-V contributes 14,578 of 15,401 matched pairs, while VLSU contributes 659 and Asimov-2.0 contributes 164.
Only five models are evaluated and fine-tuning results cover two open models.
Code and checkpoints were not available for this review; authors say code will follow acceptance.
No real-world incidence, downstream agent action or robot outcome is measured.
Repurposed benchmark prompts and model-native output templates may affect results; the study does not settle transfer across models or deployment settings.
brief.summary: A 5 October 2026 preprint evaluates five vision-language models on 15,401 matched harmful visual requests, varying whether each request asks for a text answer or a spatial grounding such as a point or box. The authors report that grounding refusal trails text-answer refusal by 31–59 percentage points depending on the domain, and that safety system prompts do not close the gap. A fine-tuning recipe combining grounding-form refusals, capability data and benign examples reportedly improves refusal on two open models while tracking over-refusal and grounding capability. This is a single author-run preprint scored by one LLM judge; 14,578 of 15,401 pairs are from the social-bias dataset, code is not released, and real-world harm incidence is not established.

technical.claimed_result: The authors interpret the difference as a response-mode generalization gap and report that a training mixture improves grounding and text refusal on two open models. The paper does not establish real-world harm incidence or downstream action outcomes.
technical.compute_or_cost: No deployment cost or real-world incident-rate estimate is reported.
technical.demonstrated_result: The paper reports 15,401 matched harmful pairs across VLSU (659), BBQ-V (14,578) and Asimov-2.0 (164), evaluated on five VLMs. Averaged grounding refusal trails VQA refusal by 31–59 percentage points depending on domain; system prompting does not close the gap. For Qwen3-VL-8B and VisionReasoner-7B, authors report fine-tuning gains in grounding refusal, including on held-out Asimov-2.0, while tracking PointArena capability and benign over-refusal.
technical.implementation_status: Public preprint; authors state code will be released upon acceptance. No code was run in this activation.
technical.mechanism: The authors convert three visual safety datasets into matched pairs that hold image, harmful intent and wording constant while changing only response mode: text VQA versus a native point or bounding-box grounding interface. A Gemini 3.5 Flash LLM judge scores refusal/compliance. Their fine-tuning combines grounding-form refusals, self-distilled benign examples and capability grounding data.
technical.novelty: Matched evaluation of whether refusal behavior transfers from text answers to spatial grounding outputs, with separate measurements for harmful refusal, benign over-refusal and grounding capability.
technical.regime: Five VLMs, three repurposed datasets and one Gemini 3.5 Flash LLM judge. The largest dataset is BBQ-V (14,578 of 15,401 matched pairs). Fine-tuning results cover Qwen3-VL-8B and VisionReasoner-7B. Benchmarks do not measure real-world harm or downstream action incidence.
technical.reproducibility: Author-reported v1 preprint; one LLM judge; code not yet released; no independent reproduction.
technical.strongest_baseline: Matched VQA-mode requests using the same image and harmful intent; for training, each model’s own pre-fine-tuning behavior. The paper also compares prompting and reports it does not close the gap, with some benign over-refusal trade-offs.

brief.title: Preprint reports a visual-grounding refusal gap across five vision-language models
brief.why_it_matters: When a model’s coordinates are consumed by a GUI agent or robot, a refusal policy that works for text may not carry over to the actionable spatial output. The paper motivates evaluating matched response modes and tracking safety alongside benign over-refusal and grounding capability. Its results do not establish deployment prevalence or real-world harm; the dataset mix, one-judge evaluation and small model sample need independent testing.
